ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Mumtaz Mahal

code.originalText: First prenatal visit at 13 weeks in a fourteenth pregnancy: dating and nuchal translucency scan, prenatal tests, and a high-risk plan

text.paragraph: First prenatal visit at 13 weeks in a fourteenth pregnancy: dating and nuchal translucency scan, prenatal tests, and a high-risk plan [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: Pregnant again soon after her last baby; tired and breathless on stairs, and unsure how far along she is. [S]
She has lost six children and wants to do everything possible for this baby and to be well enough for the children she has. [S]
Her family may travel again during the pregnancy and she wants to know when and how she can travel safely. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: She was born Arjumand Banu Begum in Agra in April 1593; an encyclopedia, citing a seventeenth-century court history, gives 27 April 1593. [D]
Her father, Abu'l-Hasan Asaf Khan, was a Persian noble; his sister was the Empress Nur Jahan, wife of the emperor Jahangir. Her mother's family came from Qazvin in Persia. [D]

She was betrothed to Prince Khurram, later the emperor Shah Jahan, in 1607, and married him on 10 May 1612; he gave her the title Mumtaz Mahal, rendered as 'Chosen One of the Palace' or 'the Exalted One of the Palace'. [D]
She was a Shi'a Muslim. [D]
Despite her frequent pregnancies, she travelled with her husband's entourage on his military campaigns. [D]

Her first thirteen children were born between 1613 and 1630: Hur-ul-Nisa (1613), Jahanara (1614), Dara Shikoh (1615), Shah Shuja (1616), Roshanara (1617), Aurangzeb (1618), Izad Bakhsh (1619), Surayya Banu (1621), a son who died soon after birth (1622), Murad Bakhsh (1624), Lutf Allah (1626), Daulat Afza (1628), and Husn Ara (1630). [D]

Six of her children died in infancy or early childhood before 1631: Hur-ul-Nisa at three and Surayya Banu at seven, both of smallpox; Izad Bakhsh in infancy; a son soon after birth in 1622; Lutf Allah at about eighteen months; and Daulat Afza in infancy. [D]
Her thirteenth child, Husn Ara, was born on 23 April 1630. [D]

In the year 1040 AH (from August 1630) the emperor was in the Deccan with the court at Burhanpur, during a severe famine in the Deccan and Gujarat, when he ordered soup kitchens and weekly alms for as long as he remained at Burhanpur. [D]

text.paragraph: 6 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

First prenatal visit: dating and nuchal translucency scan; blood count, ferritin, blood group and antibody screen, rubella immunity, hepatitis B surface antigen, HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis C tests; urine culture for asymptomatic bacteriuria; hemoglobin electrophoresis for microcytosis; hemoglobin A1c as an early diabetes screen; influenza vaccine; folic acid. Guideline: Pregnancy at Age 35 Years or Older: ACOG Obstetric Care Consensus No. 11 (2022); USPSTF A and B Recommendations (2026); Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Persons (2026) [S]

Aneuploidy screening offered, with diagnostic testing available: cell-free DNA and the nuchal translucency measurement today, or chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis; she chose cell-free DNA. Guideline: Pregnancy at Age 35 Years or Older: ACOG Obstetric Care Consensus No. 11 (2022); Screening for Fetal Chromosomal Abnormalities: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 226 (2020) [S]

Maternal-fetal medicine consultation for a fourteenth pregnancy at 37 with a short interpregnancy interval and anemia: surveillance, anemia treatment, placental assessment, delivery timing and place, and postpartum hemorrhage planning. Guideline: Pregnancy at Age 35 Years or Older: ACOG Obstetric Care Consensus No. 11 (2022); Practice Bulletin No. 183: Postpartum Hemorrhage (2017) [S]

Iron deficiency anemia: ferrous sulfate 325 mg every other day; repeat blood count and ferritin in four weeks, with intravenous iron in the second trimester if she cannot tolerate oral iron or the hemoglobin does not rise; aim for hemoglobin of 11 g/dL or more before delivery. Guideline: Anemia in Pregnancy: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 233 (2021) [S]

Preeclampsia prevention: aspirin 81 mg at bedtime from 13 weeks until delivery for two moderate risk factors (age 35 or older and a previous adverse pregnancy outcome); blood pressure and urine protein at every visit. Guideline: Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality: Preventive Medication (2021) [S]

Detailed anatomy scan at 20 to 22 weeks with placental location; if the placenta is low-lying or covers the cervix, a repeat scan at 32 weeks and assessment for placenta accreta spectrum. Guideline: Pregnancy at Age 35 Years or Older: ACOG Obstetric Care Consensus No. 11 (2022); Obstetric Care Consensus No. 7: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (2018) [S]

Gestational diabetes: hemoglobin A1c today because she is of South Asian heritage with a BMI of 23 or more; one-hour glucose challenge at 24 to 28 weeks. Guideline: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 190: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (2018) [S]

Travel: travel is reasonable until about 36 weeks if the pregnancy stays uncomplicated; on long journeys walk every one to two hours, drink plenty, and wear compression stockings; carry her prenatal record; find maternity care where she stays; stay near the delivery hospital from 36 weeks. Guideline: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 746: Air Travel During Pregnancy (2018) [S]

Postpartum hemorrhage risk assessment at intake and again in the third trimester and on admission for birth (grand multiparity and anemia raise her risk); delivery planned in a hospital with a blood bank, anesthesia, and an operating theatre. Guideline: Practice Bulletin No. 183: Postpartum Hemorrhage (2017); WHO recommendations for the prevention and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage (2012) [S]

Mood: EPDS in each trimester, with support for the grief of having lost several children. Guideline: Screening and Diagnosis of Mental Health Conditions During Pregnancy and Postpartum (Clinical Practice Guideline No. 4) (2023) [S]
Referral to maternal-fetal medicine, Adaeze Montgomery-Rahimi, MD, ordered 2026-01-06 [S]
